title: Blackface, minstrel shows and being the last coon shouter
summary: He distinguishes blackface from minstrelsy, recalls Kentucky shows, and calls himself the last coon shouter.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Lee, didn't you often attend minstrel shows and weren't you in blackface too?

Oh yes, I did blackface, not so much of the minstrel shows as I worked all over the country in theaters and nightclubs as a blackface act. And it's not a minstrel act, it's entirely different in a minstrel. Minstrel, you know, they paint around their lips white and in red blackface you don't do that. You make yourself black all over and leave your lips naturally.
Do you remember any early minstrel shows when you were a kid, very young, what they were like up in Kentucky? Do you remember any traveling shows going through there?
Oh, I can't remember the name of them but I can remember what they looked like and I used to go to see all of them. And Penrose is one of them. He used to have a blackface act out on Penrose.

Did any colored minstrel shows, I understand they have both colored and white minstrel shows in those days. Do you remember seeing ads, even if you didn't go to any colored minstrel shows, do you remember seeing any ads for them up there?
No, as far as I know, the colored minstrels didn't come to Kentucky.
I think Handy says he was with one of them for a while in later years. I just wondered if...
Well, I don't think they come to Henderson if they did, that's beyond my knowledge. I don't know anything about it. They might have, but I doubt that.
Do you remember any of the early Coonschauters that were typical of that style, people that might have made records?

No, the ones that I know and I used to see and would do that style or any ways near that, I don't know if they ever made records. If they did, I didn't know anything about it. But I did hear some when I was a very small kid singing. The fact about it, when I was a small kid, I never heard nobody sing any other way. That was a popular song. That was a popular way. And I'm the only singer today, as they tell me, that is a Coonschauter. As Sophie Tucker says, she's the last of the Red Hot Mamas, but I'm the last of the Coonschauters. I'm the modern singer of today that sings like they did during the Civil War, which is considered unusual and different. I'm the last one at sings like that, which is a style of singing during the Civil War back in the 18's.
Lee, at one time when you were in blackface, didn't you have an embarrassing experience with the cork when you were in?

Oh yes, when I first started doing blackface naturally, I didn't know anything about putting the blackface on, the cork and all this stuff. And the fact about it, it wasn't exactly a cork. I think it was a little cork and grease mixed up together. And I put it on and went out and did the dance and got to perspiring and it all just run off. And I looked like one of these Georgia watermelons.
